newsitem.title: UK: UK April PMI index 53.1, manuf up for 11th month.
newsitem.headline: UK April PMI index 53.1, manuf up for 11th month.

text.p: British manufacturing expanded for the 11th consecutive month in April and the purchasing managers' index (PMI) rose to 53.1 from 52.8 in March, the Chartered Institute of Purchasing and Supply (CIPS) said.
"Companies continued to raise output to meet further improvements in order books," the CIPS said in its Report on Business.

"Although the rate of growth of export orders again declined as a result of the sustained strength of the pound in April, any losses were largely offset by the continued buoyancy of demand for manufactured goods from domestic customers."

Overall growth in new orders remained strong as a result, although it was lower than that recorded in the latter half of last year, before the appreciation in sterling began to subdue demand for exports.
"Order levels have now risen for 11 consecutive months," the CIPS said.

Despite a substantial increase in output in April, the institute said high sales levels depleted stocks of finished goods for the second month running. "However, significant capacity pressures -- and the potential inflationary impact of supply shortages -- have yet to appear."

"Suppliers' delivery times, which tend to lengthen when demand outstrips supply, registered no overall change in April as companies encountered few problems meeting current orders within established lead-times."
With spare capacity in many sectors, more purchasing managers negotiated lower prices than faced price rises from suppliers.
The continued strength of sterling dampened export demand to some extent but also reduced the cost of imported goods.
"Consequently, the average price paid for inputs by manufacturers registered the fourth largest monthly decline recorded by this survey to date and the 18th successive monthly fall," the CIPS said.
Few firms significantly increased the size of their workforce in recent months despite the growth in sales.
"Restructuring to improve competitiveness remains commonplace and manufacturing employment expanded only slightly as a result in April."
The following are the main seasonally adjusted PMI indices, with originally reported March figures in brackets:
April March
Purchasing managers' index 53.1 52.8 (52.9)
Quantity of purchases 55.3 55.5 (55.6)
Suppliers' delivery times 50.1 48.3 (47.6)
Stocks of purchases 47.6 43.3 (43.3)
Stocks of finished goods 48.1 46.4 (46.6)
Employment 51.2 49.9 (49.4)

NOTE: The PMI is based on o weighted average of seasonally adjusted measures of output, new orders, suppliers' delivery times, stocks of items purchased and employment. A reading above 50 indicates that manufacturing is generally expanding, below 50 that it is generally contracting.
-- Richard Murphy, London Newsroom 44 171 542 2774
